chat.author: Italo Busi
chat.text:
Mahesh Jethanandani said:

@Aihua, making the type a union is reasonable solution as far as providing flexibility is concerned. It however does not address the concern that Jan raised, which is how would you check for spelling mistakes.

This information is provided by a network controller and not by an human: IMHO, spelling mistakes should be checked by the mechanisms used to provide this information to the network controller. For example, if this information is manually configured within the network controller, the network controller shall ensure there are no spelling mistakes.
Since the mechanisms used by the network controller to discover this information (e.g., manual configuration on the network controller) are outside the scope of this document also the mechanisms to perform these checks are.
Therefore, I would propose to add some text describing these assumptions in the operational considerations section.

chat.author: Mahesh Jethanandani
chat.text:
@Italo, we should probably take this to the mailing list so that Jan has a chance to chime in with his comment. 
In my mind, I suggested a spelling mistake, but maybe I should explain what I meant. If I want to discover a NE by location and I run a query where the location is a string, something like Street or St. oth valid. So a controller will not flag it as spelling error. However, the query will return one or the other NE, depending on whether the location has Street or St. in it.
